questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy presents with involuntary dancing movements of his right hand. He was diagnosed with rheumatic fever. What constitutes the ganglia involved in the presenting complication?
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Sydenham's chorea, a complication of rheumatic fever. The choreic movements are caused by the destruction of D2 neurons of the striatum. The neostriatum consists of the caudate nucleus and putamen.

The image given below shows Sydenham's chorea in a patient.



Nomenclature of basal ganglia:

  • Corpus striatum: Caudate nucleus + putamen+ globus pallidus
  • Lentiform nucleus: Putamen + globus pallidus
  • Neostriatum: Caudate nucleus + putamen







Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no. 364

questions.stem: Which of the following is false regarding the lentiform complex?

options.label: A
options.text: The internal capsule separates the lentiform complex from caudate nucleus.

options.label: B
options.text: The external capsule separates the claustrum from putamen.

options.label: C
options.text: Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the internal medullary lamina.

options.label: D
options.text: Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the external medullary lamina.

questions.answerText: Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the internal medullary lamina.
questions.solutionHtml:
Putamen and globus pallidus are separated by the external medullary lamina.

From deep to superficial, the order of structures of basal ganglia in horizontal section is as follows:

  • Caudate nucleus (innermost)
  • Internal capsule
  • Globus pallidus internal (GPi)
  • Internal medullary lamina
  • Globus pallidus external (GPe)
  • External medullary lamina
  • Putamen
  • External capsule
  • Claustrum
  • Extreme capsule
  • Insular cortex (outermost)






Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 41st Edition, Page no. 365

Wilson's pencils are thin myelinated or unmyelinated axons, which are afferents and efferents passing through the striatum.
 
The image given below shows micrograph of the putamen (top-right) and external globus pallidus (bottom-left), showing Wilson's pencils (blue, diagonal, linear structures).

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man presented with a reduced range of motion in his limbs. On examination, cogwheel rigidity and resting tremors were noticed. What is the direct pathway involved in this disorder?

options.label: A
options.text: Cortex Striatum Globus pallidus Subthalamic nucleus Premotor cortex

options.label: B
options.text: Cortex Striatum Globus pallidus Thalamus Premotor cortex

options.label: C
options.text: Cortex Globus pallidus Subthalamic nucleus Thalamus Premotor cortex

options.label: D
options.text: Cortex Globus pallidus Striatum Thalamus Premotor cortex

questions.answerText: Cortex Striatum Globus pallidus Thalamus Premotor cortex
questions.solutionHtml:
The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Parkinson's disease, a disorder involving the destruction of the substantia nigra in the basal ganglia. The most accurate representation of the direct pathway in the basal ganglia is cortex > striatum > globus pallidus> thalamus > premotor cortex. 

Parkinson's disease is a chronic progressive neurodegenerative disease that is clinically manifested by a triad of cardinal motor symptoms- rigidity, bradykinesia and tremor.

The indirect pathway is represented as follows:

Cortex > Striatum > Globus pallidus externa > Subthalamic nucleus > Globus pallidus interna and Substantia nigra reticulata >Thalamus > Premotor cortex

The direct pathway stimulates the cortex to produce movement and the indirect pathway inhibits movement.





Adam and victor's principles of neurology 10th edition, Page no. 68

questions.stem: A man presented with sudden violent flinging movements confined to the proximal parts of the right limb. This condition is caused due to the lesion involving which structure?
questions.solutionHtml:
A lesion in the subthalamic nucleus causes sudden, violent, involuntary movements confined to one side of the body, commonly affecting the proximal extremity musculature, a condition called hemiballismus. The movements are seen contralateral to the side of the lesion, i.e., involuntary movements of the right arm and leg are seen in the lesion of the left subthalamic nucleus and vice versa.





Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy, 8th edition, Page no. 167

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a part of the limbic system?
questions.solutionHtml:
Medial thalamic nuclei are not part of the limbic system. The anterior nucleus of the thalamus is a part of the limbic system.

The limbic system controls emotional behavior and is involved in the conversion of short-term memory to long-term memory. It consists of both the grey mater and white mater. It is located between the cerebral cortex and the hypothalamus.






Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy, 8th edition, Page no.301
